content:
rachel: Hey team — during a customer demo our long-running streaming job started getting 429s right at midnight UTC. UI for our org shows monthly credits refilled, but the project using the service key still shows 0 and the API returns quota_exceeded. This started right after we upgraded our plan + promo credits last week. Any ideas?

mei (Support): Sorry about the disruption. Can you paste the service key prefix (first 8 chars) and the project id? Also was the key created before or after the upgrade?

rachel: Key prefix: sk-prod-1a2b3c4d, project: acme-analytics-prod. Key was created months ago (pre-upgrade). Here's the curl we used and the returned body: 
```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-1a2b3c4d..." https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
```
Response: HTTP/1.1 429
{"error":"quota_exceeded","detail":"monthly tokens exhausted"}
UI (console) shows org monthly remaining: 420000, project acme-analytics-prod: 0.

derek (SRE): That pattern usually means the service key is drawing from a project-level quota that didn't receive the org/topup mapping during the upgrade. We have two moving parts: billing assignment and edge cache that surfaces the counts. Promo/topup sync is supposed to attach credits to existing project buckets, but older keys can be left pointing to the old bucket.

mei (Support): Can you run the usage endpoint and paste the redacted result? Example: 
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-1a2b3c4d..." "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/usage?scope=project&project=acme-analytics-prod"
```
(please redact tokens and any PII)

rachel: Pasted the snippet: {"project":"acme-analytics-prod","window":"2026-05","used":120000,"limit":0} — that limit 0 looks wrong.

derek (SRE): yep. limit 0 means project bucket not assigned any refill. Two quick checks: (1) whether the project is set to "inherit org credits" in Billing -> Projects. (2) whether the service key is scoped to a project bucket vs org token.

mei (Support): I'm opening an internal ticket and invalidating the quota cache for that project now. Workarounds in the meantime: (A) switch the job to an org-level token (sk-org-xxxx) which will draw from the org bucket, or (B) reassign the project's billing to inherit org credits via Console -> Settings -> Billing -> Billing inheritance. We'll attempt a manual attach of the promo to the project's bucket. ETA ~ 15-30m for the cache invalidation + sync.

oncall-eng: FYI infra: there is a background sync job that pushes org-level promo/topups down to project buckets on a 1-hour cadence. Plan-change events trigger an immediate sync only for newly created keys. Existing keys sometimes require manual migration if assignment metadata is missing. We'll patch the sync to be immediate for all existing buckets soon.

usage-bot: incident #INC-20260501-87 created by mei (P2) — quota-mapping-missing for project acme-analytics-prod.

rachel: I changed the background job to use an org token as a quick test, and the 429s stopped within a minute. Looks recovered for the demo. :tada:

mei (Support): Closing the customer-facing loop: root cause = project-level quota bucket did not inherit the org promo/topup because the billing assignment record was missing after the plan change. Fixes applied: 
- invalidated project quota cache (done)
- manually attached promo/topup to project bucket (done)
- migrated mapping for existing service keys so legacy keys point to the updated bucket (done)
Notes / recommendations: if you need immediate mapping in the future either create a new service key after a plan change or temporarily switch to an org-level token. We'll follow up with a short postmortem and an infra change to trigger full sync on plan-change.

derek (SRE): I'll add a playbook item to ensure the sync is kicked for all existing buckets on plan-change and to add monitoring for mismatches (project showing 0 while org >0).

rachel: Confirmed — no more 429s after switching back to the original key. Thanks everyone for the quick help :heart:
